Project Summary: AstroGuard Health
What We Developed:
AstroGuard Health is an interactive, web-based visual dashboard designed to help astronauts monitor, assess, and manage their physical and mental well-being during long-duration space missions. The platform features a dynamic astronaut telemetry monitor, an interactive anatomical body map with color-coded risk indicators, real-time time-series charts tracking vital signs (such as heart rate, blood sugar, and sleep), and a gamified daily mission routine checklist.
How It Addresses the Challenge:
The software directly tackles the challenge of autonomous healthcare in space by integrating NASA’s Human Research Program data on the five spaceflight hazards (radiation, isolation, gravity changes, distance, and hostile environments). When a metric drifts out of safe thresholds, the tool provides immediate, easy-to-understand explanations and actionable countermeasures, empowering astronauts to evaluate and treat conditions without relying solely on ground control.
Why It Is Important:
As humanity embarks on Artemis lunar bases and future Mars missions, communication delays with Earth make crew self-reliance vital. AstroGuard Health bridges the gap between complex medical data and rapid decision-making, mitigating risks like bone density loss and behavioral fatigue to safeguard crew health and mission success.
details:
What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

AstroGuard Health is an interactive, mission-control-style web dashboard that acts as an autonomous health companion for astronauts on long-duration space missions (such as lunar bases or Mars transits).

  • The Workflow: Astronauts log daily health indicators—including heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, sleep duration, and mood/behavioral notes—either manually or through simulated telemetry feeds.
  • Interactive Body Map & Visual Alerts: The software features an SVG-based anatomical interface. When an astronaut clicks a specific region (e.g., bones/joints for gravity loss, or the head/brain for isolation stress), the UI highlights relevant risks tied to NASA’s Five Hazards of Human Spaceflight (radiation, isolation, altered gravity,distance, and hostile closed environments).
  • Dynamic Analysis & Guidance: Color-coded indicators (Green for nominal, Yellow for caution, Red for critical) immediately flag out-of-range metrics. The system then delivers step-by-step guidance, countermeasure protocols,and treatment recommendations, reducing reliance on delayed ground control.

2. What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Autonomous Self-Assessment: Empowers crew members to catch early warning signs of bone density loss,immune suppression, or cardiovascular strain on their own.
  • Reduced Cognitive Load: Translates dense medical data and telemetry into clear, intuitive visual cues, ensuring tired or isolated astronauts can digest critical information quickly.
  • Proactive Routine Maintenance: Keeps crew members engaged through structured daily wellness checklists and gamified mission milestones.

3. What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?

As space missions extend further from Earth (e.g., Artemis and Mars exploration), communication blackouts and signal delays make real-time medical support from Earth impossible. AstroGuard Health bridges this gap by ensuring crew health is continuously monitored, interpreted, and managed locally. By mitigating minor health degradation before it becomes critical, the project safeguards both astronaut well-being and overall mission success.

4. What Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, or Software Were Used?

  • Frontend & UI Framework: React.js / Next.js paired with Tailwind CSS for a responsive, futuristic mission-control aesthetic.
  • Animations & Interactivity: Framer Motion for smooth screen transitions and SVG vector manipulation for the interactive body map.
  • Data Visualization: Recharts or Chart.js for rendering dynamic time-series graphs tracking health indicators over mission days.
  • Backend & Data Storage (Optional/Mock): Node.js with lightweight JSON storage or Python (FastAPI) to parse NASA open datasets and simulate data logs.
  • Cloud & Infrastructure (Global Offers): Hosted via Microsoft Azure or Google Cloud Platform (GCP) using hackathon credits, with a custom domain registered through GoDaddy/Porkbun.

5. How Is Your Project Creative?

AstroGuard Health reimagines standard clinical health trackers by framing them through the lens of deep-space exploration. Instead of presenting raw spreadsheets or boring data tables, it turns human anatomy into an interactive diagnostic canvas. By integrating game-like daily habit loops, color-coded threat matrices, and immediate contextual guidance tied directly to NASA’s research parameters, it transforms a chore into an engaging, mission-critical tool.

6. What Factors Did Your Team Consider?

  • Extreme Environments & Usability: Astronauts operate under high-stress, high-fatigue conditions. The UI was designed with high-contrast color coding, large touch targets, and minimal text density to prevent cognitive overload.
  • Data Privacy & Local-First Resiliency: Because deep-space communication is unstable, the architecture prioritizes local offline caching of vital logs, ensuring the crew can evaluate their health even if telemetry synchronization with Earth is temporarily lost.
  • Scientific Grounding: Every threshold, hazard category, and recommendation was mapped directly to NASA’s Human Research Program (HRP) guidelines to maintain strict scientific validity and realism.
